messages.author: 146bc26797d1c5e2
messages.subject: ADVI
parts:
I guess some are willing to try the ADVI algorithm, http://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.03431.pdf, currently available in Github in some developer branches for the cmdStan interface. Below is what I did to get it apparently working:

1. git clone https://github.com/stan-dev/cmdstan.git -b feature/advi-command

2. In the cmdstan directory, "make stan-revert". (With "make stan-update/develop" I ended up having no math library.)

3. "make manual", then read the short chapter on variational estimation.

4. "make examples/bernoulli/bernoulli"

5. Within the bernoulli directory, first " ./bernoulli sample data file=bernoulli.data.R" to make sure Stan is working in general, then "./bernoulli variational data file=bernoulli.data.R"

I understand ADVI is experimental and any kind of support is limited, etc. I'm just eager to try it with some models that are slow with NUTS.

Thanks for making it available.

messages.author: 146bc26797d1c5e2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] ADVI
parts:
Intialization with the current ADVI (develop branch) seems to be difficult at times. I have a model with a Cholesky-factor correlation matrix, and while NUTS sometimes complains at the beginning, it samples eventually fine. The LBFGS optimiser similarly reports a few non-finite gradient at first, then starts to iterate.

With this model, the mean field ADVI seems to evaluate ELBO to nan quite often, then eventually crashes with 

"Exception: stan::variational::normal_meanfield::set_mu: Input vector[1] is nan, but must not be nan!"

This is with init=0, which works better than random initialisation. Playing with ADVI parameters (number of gradient samples, eta) does not help much. More diagonal LKJ prior maybe helps a bit. 

Gradient seems to be fine when I look at it with "diagnose init=0". At least there are no infinities or eye-popping differences between the gradient and the finite approximation. Some gradient components are zero, for missing value "parameters" of the model. (They are not zero with init=1.)

With init=2, ADVI constantly fails without reporting any iteration steps (even when eval_elbo=1). 

I don't know what happens at the initialisation phase in general, but ADVI code does not seem to have any retries or checks for failed gradients? (I only took a quick look at the advi.hpp file, so could be wrong.)

(This is not critical for me in any way, just wanted to share the observation in case it helps with development.)

messages.author: 146bc26797d1c5e2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] ADVI
parts:
To me, with the experience of a single model :), this seems similar kind of initialisation issue that sometimes happens with optimisation and NUTS, and is cured by restarts. It has two parts. 

One is failed elbo evaluation: it reports a NaN, maybe because one or more elbo samples return nan. The iteration still continues. Would it make sense to reject the nan samples, and maybe continue sampling until the configured number of (elbo) samples succeeds? This would introduce a bias, but that's ok if the problem disappears when the iteration continues. 

The other issue that crashes the iteration with the set_mu exception looks like a gradient failure. That would be a place for a restart.

Ordinary non-convergence is usually a reason to tune eta or other parameters.

On Wednesday, July 15, 2015 at 12:08:38 PM UTC+3, Dustin Tran wrote:
We can certainly do this too; the analog of this for variational inference is to redo the optimization up to 100 times if none of the previous initializations converged. How do you guys determine when to restart the MCMC again?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] ADVI
parts:
On Wednesday, July 15, 2015 at 5:08:38 AM UTC-4, Dustin Tran wrote:
> Calculating densities and/or gradients can throw exceptions.
> What do you do with those exceptions?
Nothing so far. The checks/error messages written in the ADVI code have only been on dimension-matching.

I tried this with a student's project and we were running into exceptions where it looks like the gradient had NaNs or Infinities. Then we tried increasing grad_samples to something greater than 1 in hopes that would overcome the problem but it seems to just average the gradient samples, in which case if there is a NaN in any of them then it will throw. Is it possible to make a quick patch somewhere to exclude non-finite gradients from the average?

Ben

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] ADVI
parts:
I submitted a pull request, which adds the checks for NaN/infinity immediately after calls to the model’s log probability or gradient. 

On throwing NaN/infinity-evaluated samples: This is certainly doable, although I’m not sure if we should be doing this. In principle, this shouldn’t happen for any samples; and if one occurred, then there’s something wrong with the underlying parameter space we’re searching over. (Or perhaps it’s a numerical issue?) We can throw a warning perhaps. Not sure what the convention is for the rest of Stan?

Dustin

On Wednesday, July 15, 2015 at 4:19:22 PM UTC-4, Dustin Tran wrote:
On throwing NaN/infinity-evaluated samples: This is certainly doable, although I’m not sure if we should be doing this. In principle, this shouldn’t happen for any samples; and if one occurred, then there’s something wrong with the underlying parameter space we’re searching over. (Or perhaps it’s a numerical issue?) We can throw a warning perhaps. Not sure what the convention is for the rest of Stan?

Stan's MCMC stuff presumes that it is a numerical issue, assigns zero probability to those parameters, and continues on. In this case, I'm pretty sure it is an numerical issue with the gradient (albeit perhaps an intractable one) because it always occurred between 100 and 200 optimization steps and none of the unconstrained parameters were outside (-3,3) when it stopped.

Ben
